title: Depths of Mendoza
brief: Original-IP fps-narrative game (sub-genre: fps-narrative). Capture the core mechanics and game-feel of "Bioshock" (critically acclaimed, 96%) — but with your OWN original name, theme, characters and art. Do NOT reference or reuse that title's IP. SIGNATURE MECHANIC for this genre: . MUST SHIP COMPLETE: a working menu (title + difficulty + how-to + settings via FFG.Shell), the page control bar (fullscreen/mute/pause), a clear win AND lose state, readable HUD, and polished feel — it must play start-to-finish with no manual fixes.

M1.done_when: core loop genuinely playable in ONE level: structure+feel green, no crash

design_doc.title: Depths of Mendoza
design_doc.core_loop: You are a deep-sea salvage worker exploring the sunken ruins of Mendoza Station, a 1960s underwater research facility that experimented with neural-enhancement drugs derived from bioluminescent organisms. Navigate claustrophobic corridors, hack security systems to unlock new areas, scavenge resources to craft ammunition and genetic augmentations, and survive encounters with mutated researchers using a combination of makeshift weapons (rivet gun, electro-harpoon, flare launcher) and psychic powers (telekinesis, neural shock, bioluminescent decoy). Each room tells a story through environmental details and audio logs. Combat is tactical: choose stealth or aggression, set traps using the environment (electrified water, explosive canisters), and decide whether to harvest or rescue mutated survivors for different upgrade paths.
design_doc.scope: IN: 5 interconnected station modules (Hydroponics, Medical, Engineering, Residential, Command), 3 weapon types with alt-fire modes, 4 psychic powers with upgrade trees, hacking mini-game (pattern-matching lock), moral choice system (harvest vs rescue affects ending), 8-12 hour campaign, resource scarcity economy, audio logs and environmental storytelling, boss encounter at Command module. OUT: multiplayer, procedural generation, open world, vehicle sections, companion NPCs, branching narrative paths (linear story with one moral axis), crafting beyond ammo/medkits, base building, New Game+.
design_doc.art_direction: Palette: Deep ocean blues (#0a1929, #1e3a5f), sickly bioluminescent greens (#39ff14, #7fff00), rusted industrial oranges (#d2691e, #8b4513), blood reds for danger (#8b0000). Mood: Oppressive isolation meets art-deco retrofuturism. Corroded brass fixtures, shattered aquarium glass, flickering neon signage in Cyrillic-inspired script, grotesque bio-organic growths spreading through sterile labs. Lighting is key: player flashlight cuts through murky darkness, enemy bioluminescence telegraphs threats, sparking machinery creates danger zones. Underwater pressure and creaking metal ambience build dread.

milestone_plan.M1: Vertical slice: Single Medical module room playable start-to-finish. Player spawns, finds rivet gun, encounters one splicer enemy type, uses telekinesis to throw object, hacks one door, reaches exit. Lighting and audio establish mood. ~3 minutes of core loop.
milestone_plan.M2: Full mechanics: All 3 weapons functional with alt-fire, all 4 powers implemented, hacking mini-game working, harvest/rescue choice implemented with UI feedback, upgrade station menu functional, enemy AI for 3 enemy types (Splicer, Turret, Big Daddy analog), health/ammo/resource pickup system.
milestone_plan.M3: Content complete: All 5 station modules built and connected, environmental storytelling placed (10+ audio logs, readable notes, visual set-pieces), full critical path playable, final boss encounter implemented, both endings (harvest vs rescue) functional, difficulty scaling tuned.
milestone_plan.M4: Polish pass: HUD redesign for clarity (health/ammo/power meter/objective marker), SFX for all interactions, music track for each module + combat sting, particle effects for powers and weapons, screen shake and hit feedback, save/load system, pause menu with settings (volume sliders, sensitivity, difficulty change), tutorial tooltips for first 10 minutes.
milestone_plan.M5: Ship-ready: FFG.Shell integration (title screen, difficulty select, how-to-play screen, settings panel), page control bar (fullscreen toggle, mute, pause overlay), win screen (escape Mendoza + your moral outcome stats), lose screen (retry from checkpoint), performance optimization (60fps target), bug fixing, QA pass on all 3 difficulties, build export and upload.

definition_of_done: Player can start from title screen, select difficulty (Easy/Normal/Hard), and reach end credits without manual intervention
All 3 weapons and 4 psychic powers are unlockable and functional with unique SFX and VFX
Harvest vs Rescue choice appears at least 5 times; final ending reflects cumulative moral score
Win state: Escape pod cutscene plays after defeating final boss; lose state: death screen offers retry from last checkpoint
HUD clearly displays health bar, ammo count, active power, and current objective at all times
Settings menu allows volume adjust, mouse sensitivity, and difficulty swap mid-game without breaking state
At least 8 audio logs discoverable that explain Mendoza Station backstory and the genetic experiments
Hacking mini-game appears on 10+ doors; failure triggers alarm and spawns reinforcements
Page control bar allows fullscreen toggle, mute, and pause (gameplay freezes, overlay appears) at any moment
No placeholder assets: all models, textures, sounds are original or licensed; no 'TODO' or debug text visible to player
Game runs at stable 60fps on mid-range hardware (tested); no soft-locks or progression blockers in critical path
Three difficulty modes alter enemy damage, resource scarcity, and aim assist in measurable ways
